verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim documents a ROS Bridge and validating robot stacks with ROS 2, including loading worlds, spawning entities and stepping sims through ROS 2 services. It also offers software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, and Isaac ROS packages deploy to Jetson. Together these imply a ROS 2 stack can target both sim and real hardware, but no documentation states that the same code runs on both without changes. The community report of sim-to-real physics drift concerns behavioral fidelity, not code portability, so it does not dispute this story. Missing for 10: an explicit documented sim-to-real code-portability workflow (same nodes and launch configs swapped between sim and hardware), and hands-on or independent corroboration of running unchanged code on a real robot.
